mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.0% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE above 3.5% and PAYEMS above 0.3% month-over-month indicates strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and supports corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their respective 3-month moving averages signals weakening housing and overall demand, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent FEDFUNDS rate below 1.0% for six consecutive months signals an extended period of monetary accommodation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A YoY increase in RSAFS above 5% signals a surge in personal savings, which, in the absence of corresponding consumption growth, suggests precautionary behavior and weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
